The week got off to a bad start, though, with a bad cold. I was going to be working 15 hours on Tuesday and I was a block away from home and I got a call saying they were closing early. Why?  Because there was a lady with a cold, too, at the hospital, so she couldn’t make calls. Now they had a policy now not to work on close to your home if you are sick. Bad night, Tuesday.

Aside from that, by Thursday, I’m usually completely burned out, thanks to three months of hard work. I’m getting more writing done instead of thinking about writing, and I’m sleeping in a lot more hours in a row every night thanks to my extended naps on Sunday.

With that in mind, let me say again how much I like the Kindle, and what I love about an eReader. It’s not in any fashion like an old PC or a Mac. It can be a fantastic machine if you don’t look at it like an Apple, and can instead look at it as a whole, and get the best from it.

Now. After all the work you have put into your painting, it’s time to make it available for everyone to see! Take a measurement from the top of the canvas to the bottom – that is going to be your cutting mark! Now center this on your page. Put a dot on the edge of your bottom of your standing leg (6 inches from the bottom). A ruler and a pencil will be a real help here. On your piece of paper, put the pencil an inch off from edge of your paper. With your circle, trace a circle around your inch mark. Now, then use a ruler to extend the edges of your inch mark and your length of the paper. Now take your  inch mark, bend it upward, and without straightening it, “fold” both inches farther from your inch mark. This is going to mark your corner of your painting.

Click on the enlarged image to down load a version larger than a 8 by 10. If you are using a larger piece of paper, use this as a guide.
